tutorials.problem:
Consider the graph of the parabola ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/f218c572691a74963cd3808bf4df2923122e84b65d1fabf1138bab6264b043b5.svg) shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/450251899f728a3cc927b72fdb7655204828c8e0be0432cb08cee2462d6e5bfe.png)

We can describe many features of the graph using mathematical terminology:

- The ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/fcc5df999e3b49fae1685ee0ab5bd03709804e1dd49f2ee722c4269eb0f5506d.svg)-intercepts of the parabola are at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/8171bb8403bd612f56ef5f32f400f1aef8efeed51ea279d36779771fdea1ae0d.svg) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/779cec712506e0f798805963ab85841b46650fb22681d97a64aec4b85a47d07f.svg) We say that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/b064281df4bef2506521322c7477468b9cc565616e2c5b6f21000df6522399c1.svg) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/1fb9f2f73a09599931892c1dee7629975b4d851e5dd6f0d07b7c641bbf17bf54.svg) are the **roots** (or **zeros**) of the parabola.

- The parabola intersects the ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/1d9b846cface9f9348e4081a0dd87dd254bf26663c12aa0d1a15aa24d2393261.svg)-axis at  ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/6a0e2cbf9f56c3c989ad96f020fe8bb0f7c785ff6de8073c476232b95476ac13.svg). We say that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/78d4465d85b55cee3832a9b598a2564b6a3fa9a072de8a1fb4b40ca884079670.svg) is the **![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/1d9b846cface9f9348e4081a0dd87dd254bf26663c12aa0d1a15aa24d2393261.svg)-intercept**. The ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/1d9b846cface9f9348e4081a0dd87dd254bf26663c12aa0d1a15aa24d2393261.svg)-intercept is the same as the constant term of the function.

- The parabola has a "turning point" at  ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/ef43561f9d825c9e79fb03dffafa744d386d0c2a5a07da903675bca120d59fd1.svg) which is called the **vertex**. In an upwards parabola (like the one shown above), the vertex is the minimum point, while in a downwards parabola, the vertex is the maximum point.

- The vertical line  ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/df9822243c11ec9f0fabca5cc578976d0bdea2c521b4f61964f5f3850a970504.svg) that passes through the vertex is called the **axis of symmetry**. The part of the parabola to the left of the axis of symmetry is the mirror image of the right, and vice versa.

- This particular parabola is **upward opening** because it has a distinctive ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/13ab0b72e7963f3e74404b8b75f12654ece94c2c44e1fb09fdf230b976eb681b.svg) shape. A parabola ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/7c49eede8f0eb80dadd8384ae942dc8248ef454eeb6afa1aeba7ae48e7545456.svg) is upward opening if the quadratic coefficient is positive ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/d2a0fc4d90b45e06999c89b1a40ff6f01116e9c429c195adbfced573f9e47660.svg)

- Parabolas can also be **downward opening** with a distinctive ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/57872695daf3067460adec5a506cfb1457729de4eeac879eab9f7355570bac11.svg) shape. A parabola ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/7c49eede8f0eb80dadd8384ae942dc8248ef454eeb6afa1aeba7ae48e7545456.svg) is downward opening if the quadratic coefficient is negative ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/a16d199f292dbd74941402b3d485cf107a7a985d28aeb13ab50ff6baf87f2d4b.svg)

Let's take a look at an example of a downward opening parabola.

- The ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/fcc5df999e3b49fae1685ee0ab5bd03709804e1dd49f2ee722c4269eb0f5506d.svg)-intercepts of the parabola are at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/8171bb8403bd612f56ef5f32f400f1aef8efeed51ea279d36779771fdea1ae0d.svg) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/779cec712506e0f798805963ab85841b46650fb22681d97a64aec4b85a47d07f.svg) We say that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/b064281df4bef2506521322c7477468b9cc565616e2c5b6f21000df6522399c1.svg) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/1fb9f2f73a09599931892c1dee7629975b4d851e5dd6f0d07b7c641bbf17bf54.svg) are the **roots** (or **zeros**) of the parabola.

- The parabola intersects the ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/1d9b846cface9f9348e4081a0dd87dd254bf26663c12aa0d1a15aa24d2393261.svg)-axis at  ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/6a0e2cbf9f56c3c989ad96f020fe8bb0f7c785ff6de8073c476232b95476ac13.svg). We say that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/78d4465d85b55cee3832a9b598a2564b6a3fa9a072de8a1fb4b40ca884079670.svg) is the **![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/1d9b846cface9f9348e4081a0dd87dd254bf26663c12aa0d1a15aa24d2393261.svg)-intercept**. The ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/1d9b846cface9f9348e4081a0dd87dd254bf26663c12aa0d1a15aa24d2393261.svg)-intercept is the same as the constant term of the function.

- The parabola has a "turning point" at  ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/ef43561f9d825c9e79fb03dffafa744d386d0c2a5a07da903675bca120d59fd1.svg) which is called the **vertex**. In an upwards parabola (like the one shown above), the vertex is the minimum point, while in a downwards parabola, the vertex is the maximum point.

- The vertical line  ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/df9822243c11ec9f0fabca5cc578976d0bdea2c521b4f61964f5f3850a970504.svg) that passes through the vertex is called the **axis of symmetry**. The part of the parabola to the left of the axis of symmetry is the mirror image of the right, and vice versa.
